messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Choi <susan.choi@opsmart.com>
Date: 2026-04-02T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Contract conversation: scaling runway and capacity

Hi Susan,

Hope you had a smooth quarter close. I was looking at Opsmart's upcoming renewal window (June 1) and wanted to start a conversation about scaling runway and committed capacity. Q1 traffic trends you shared indicate a sustained 2–2.5x peak increase on inference tokens during promotional events — which maps to the capacity constraints we discussed last quarter.

High-level ask: would Opsmart be open to a committed capacity increase (2.5x baseline) and a 12-month term to lock predictable pricing and reserved throughput? On our side we can propose a hybrid model (reserved + burst credits) to avoid throttling during promotional spikes.

If you agree, we can run a short benchmark with our Dedicated configuration (same model family you run) and I'll follow up with a commercial outline. Attaching the capacity worksheet so we can align on traffic windows.

Attachments: ops_capacity_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,

Ben / team,

Quick update from the bench run we spun up (48-hour representative replay):
- Configuration: Dedicated x4 (A100-equivalent), 128-token KV cache warmup, continuous batching tuned to their 512-token median sequence.
- Observations: p95 latency remained ~120ms; p99 spiked to ~320ms under sustained peaks. Token unit cost (reserved) estimates are 28% lower than their incumbent at baseline, but competitor quote we sourced is ~30% cheaper on unit price for burst-only usage (no guaranteed reserved throughput).

Interpretation: Redwood delivers more consistent latency under sustained load; competitor can offer lower headline unit price but exposes Opsmart to higher latency risk during promo surges. Recommend a blended commercial:
1) Reserved baseline at 2.0x (cheaper per unit) + 0.5x burst credits to cover spikes.
2) 12-month committed term with a 15% committed discount off list for reserved capacity.
3) One-time migration credit (equivalent to one month of reserved capacity) and a 60-day SLA addendum with faster support response for promotional windows.

Attached is a short benchmark summary you can use in the customer deck.

Attachments: benchmark-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Choi <susan.choi@opsmart.com>, Procurement Opsmart <procurement@opsmart.com>, Danielle Park <danielle.park@opsmart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-04T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal: committed capacity + hybrid burst — Opsmart renewal window

Hi Susan / Danielle / Procurement team,

Thanks for sharing the traffic sample and for letting us run the representative benchmark. Based on the run and internal pricing, Redwood can offer the following commercial that balances latency predictability and unit economics:

Summary proposal (high level):
- Committed reserved capacity: 2.0x baseline throughput (Reserved Dedicated pool)
- Burst credits: 0.5x baseline available for promotional peaks (auto-burst when reserved exhausted)
- Term: 12 months
- Commercial: 15% committed discount on reserved unit price; burst usage at a slightly higher unit price but with a burst cap to control spend
- One-time migration credit: equal to one month of reserved fees (to offset migration run costs)
- SLA addendum: 60-day elevated support for promotional windows + faster incident response (details attached)

Why this works: Redwood preserves lower p99 latency under sustained load via reserved capacity (we saw p99 spikes with competitor approaches), while the burst pool prevents throttling during unforeseen peaks. The migration credit and SLA addendum reduce Opsmart's transition risk.

Next steps:
1) If this commercial is acceptable, I'll send a formal counterproposal via DocuSign and a short MOP (migration plan) with dates.
2) Proposed internal acceptance deadline: EOD 2026-04-11 to lock pricing and capacity for the June 1 start.

Attachments: counterproposal-opsmart-20260404.pdf (pdf); SLA-addendum.pdf (pdf)
Related links: https://docusign.example/opsmart-counterproposal, https://hubspot.example/deal/OP-2026-042

We'd like to get Opsmart on a call tomorrow morning to run the pricing line items live — are you available?

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
